title: gusto out/manifest.json, version 1
description: The record of a run: a SHA-256 of job.json and of every file in out/ except this one and its signature, the gate's verdict, what the harness did, and who the runner says stands behind it. `gusto verify` re-hashes the files against it. A runner with a key signs these exact bytes in out/manifest.sig, described by schema/signature/v1.json. A reader ignores a field it does not know.

version.description: The format of this file. A file without it is version 1. A reader refuses a version newer than it knows.

job.description: The SHA-256 of job.json, as 64 lowercase hex digits.

files.description: Every regular file in out/ except manifest.json and manifest.sig, sorted by name. The signature is made over this file after it is written, so this file cannot hold its hash. A file here that is gone or changed, or a file in out/ that is not here, fails verification.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file's bytes, as 64 lowercase hex digits.

gate.description: The gate's verdict, the same one out/gates.json holds. Absent when the job had no gate to run: a turn in a conversation is not a claim that anything passed.

command.description: The gate that ran: the program and its arguments.

passed.description: Whether the gate exited zero. This, not the harness, decides the job.

harness.description: The name of the adapter that ran. A name is not a configuration: harnessDigest says which configured harness it was.

harnessDigest.description: The digest of the configured harness that ran, taken from the files the job carried before the harness started: "sha256:" and 64 lowercase hex digits, computed as docs/FORMATS.md describes. Two runs with the same digest ran the same configured harness; two with the same harness name need not have. Absent in a manifest written before it was recorded, which a reader reports as "no digest recorded" rather than inventing one.

harnessVersion.description: The agent's build: the npm package and version the runner image installed, as package@version, read from the image's /etc/gusto/harnesses. Absent where the agent was installed by hand, on a person's own computer.

harnessExit.description: The harness's exit code. A harness reporting success is a claim; the gate is the check.

stoppedAtBudget.description: Whether the harness was killed because the budget's seconds ran out.

stoppedBy.description: Who told the run to stop before it ended on its own: the person who stopped it, or a signal when nobody is named. Absent when the run was not stopped.

modelUnanswered.description: Present when the run asked its model and the proxy, in out/proxy.jsonl, saw no call to a model answered. Calls a spending cap refused are not counted. A turn with no gate that has this failed, whatever the harness's exit.

calls.description: How many calls to a model the run made: one or more.

reason.description: What went wrong with the last of them, as the proxy saw it.

stoppedByCap.description: The spending cap that stopped the run, read from out/proxy.jsonl: the proxy refused the harness's next call to a model once it was spent. Absent when no cap refused anything.

cap.description: Which cap: the job's own budget.usd, or its team's monthly cap from the operator's spend policy.

team.description: The team whose cap it was. Absent for the job's own cap.

spentUsd.description: What the proxy had counted against the cap when it refused, in US dollars. It can exceed the cap by the calls that were already in flight.

reason.description: Why, in words for the person who asked for the job.

modelEndpoint.description: The address the harness talked to, as the rules checked it. Empty when the harness needs no model.

tokens.description: The tokens the harness reported, or null when it reported none. Null is not zero: nothing reported is nothing claimed.

costUsd.description: The cost in US dollars the harness reported, or null when it reported none.

signer.description: Who the runner says stands behind the run: GUSTO_SIGNER on the runner; with no name, the id of the key it signs with; with neither, "unsigned". It is the runner's own word: a verifier names the signer from its keyring and out/manifest.sig, never from this field.

atUnix.description: When the manifest was written, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

session.description: What the harness calls the conversation this run was a turn in. Absent for a one-shot job.
